chapter: Ellington, the South, bebop and radio
title: Working with Fats Waller and Clarence Page in Cincinnati
summary: Fats Waller did a radio show and used Clarence Page's band for outside work, with Una Mae Carlisle also in the band; Dickenson found Fats fun to work with.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Was that stage shows and stuff like that?
No, he did a radio... He was doing a radio show, and he had three or four characters on there. But after the show, he had a lot of work outside, and he used a band -- and I was in there playing.
This was a band that he picked up.

Well, he fronted this band sort of like, yeah. The band was Clarence Page's band. Clarence Page just died about a month or two ago. But at that time, he was fronting the band. You know he hired the band and they played with him. And Una Mae Carlisle was in there... I've got a clipping somewhere from my home town about me and Una Mae. We both were singing in Speed Webb's band. I've got it around here somewhere, like I've got that record. This (?) I have...
The clipping. I've got it (?) somewhere. Takes a little time to find.
Was he interesting to work with, Fats?
Oh, yeah. He was a lot of fun.
